[MUQATIL:11:110-112/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Muhammad and those who repented from shirk must persevere in monotheism without disobeying God in it.
[AKHFASH:v1p391/r1] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | تطغوا comes from طغوت تطغا, like محوت تمحا.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#4/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Istaqim means continue along what you were commanded.
[TAB-FULL:v12p598/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Muhammad must remain steadfast in the religion and call to it as God commanded, and those who returned with him must obey God after disbelief.
[TAB-FULL:v12p598/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Do not transgress God's command by doing what He forbade; God sees and knows every act of obedience or disobedience, and nothing is hidden from Him.
[TAB-FULL:v12p598/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · سفيان بن عيينة | reports | Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna interprets steadfastness as remaining upon the Qur'an.
[TAB-FULL:v12p598/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd defines transgression as opposing God and committing disobedience.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Those who repent with the Prophet must also remain upright.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Uprightness includes refusing to imitate, praise, socialize with, or inwardly approve the unjust, while continuing to forbid wrongdoing and avoid unlawful wealth.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Every moment should be filled with worship; losing even one moment of an obligatory or voluntary act is a grave regret and loss.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Uprightness is continuing along one direction, unlike turning into divergent paths to the right or left.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r10] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | reports | Another interpretation is simply not to go beyond God's command.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r11] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | God sees human deeds, none of which are hidden from Him; He knew what people would do before they acted.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | The command is to persist in obeying the Lord's command and calling people to Him as the Quran directs.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Although addressed to the Prophet, the command is intended for his community.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · السدي | reports | The command is addressed to the Prophet but intended for his community.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | من تاب معك can be nominative by coordination with the subject of فاستقم, coordination with the subject of أمرت, or as a new sentence with an implied command to be upright.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Those who repented with the Prophet are his companions who turned away from polytheism.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | طغيان means exceeding the proper limit.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r8] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Do not be arrogant toward anyone; be humble before God.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r9] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Do not exceed God's revealed limits by declaring lawful or unlawful what He did not command.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r5] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The Prophet must persist in obeying his Lord and calling people to him, as the Qur'an commanded; his companions must also persist.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r6] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The companions should remain humble before God and avoid behaving arrogantly toward anyone.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r7] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God sees all human actions, and none are hidden from him.
[JISHUMI:v5p3576/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The common reading of زلفا has ḍamma on zāy and fatḥa on lām; Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Mujāhid have other vocalizations, all dialect variants.
[JISHUMI:v5p3576/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Istiqāma is continuing along one direction; the word derives from q-w-m and belongs with forms such as aqāma and istaqāma.
[JISHUMI:v5p3576/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Ṭughyān is exceeding limits in disobedience or corruption; water and floods are described this way by analogy, and the root has variant forms.
[JISHUMI:v5p3576/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The tāʾ in أمرت is a passive subject in the nominative, and ومن تاب coordinates with it; زلفا is accusative as an adverb of time.
[JISHUMI:v5p3576/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says no verse was harder on the Prophet than the command to remain upright, and that Sūrat Hūd and its sisters made him old.
[JISHUMI:v5p3579/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Uprightness in religion is obligatory and consists of performing obligations and avoiding prohibitions; repentance for past sins is valid only with commitment to future duties.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Do not transgress means neither disobey God’s command nor exceed what He commanded and forbade.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God sees all their actions and nothing is hidden from Him.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says no verse weighed more heavily on the Prophet; he said Hud and its sister chapters had made him gray.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أبو هريرة | reports | Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s teaching that religion is easy; do not overburden yourselves, but act moderately, rejoice, and seek help at different times of day and night.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Steadfastness means remaining on the Lord’s religion, practicing it, and calling others to it; those who believe with Muhammad must also remain steadfast.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar defines steadfastness as keeping to commands and prohibitions without twisting away like a fox.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · سفيان بن عبد الله الثقفي | reports | Sufyan ibn Abd Allah asked the Prophet for a concise instruction; he replied, “Say I believe in God, then be steadfast.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Although the Prophet is already upright, the command means to continue and remain steadfast, like telling someone already walking or eating to keep doing so; the address includes him and the Companions who repented from disbelief, and by implication the whole community.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | A scholar reportedly saw the Prophet in a dream and asked what in Hud made him say it and its companion suras had made him gray; the Prophet answered, 'Be steadfast as you were commanded.' Ibn Atiyya says the well-known explanation is his fear that earlier peoples' fates might befall this community.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | أمرت is an honorific plural form of address; ومن is coordinated with the pronoun in فاستقم, permitted without repeating it because كما أمرت makes the phrase long.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | ولا تطغوا means do not exceed God's limits; طغيان is crossing the limit, as with the flood and Pharaoh, or specifically letting blessings lead to transgression. | mentions 69:11, 20:24, 20:43, 79:17
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read تعملون with second-person tāʾ; Hasan and al-A'mash read يعملون with third-person yāʾ, and readers vary between open and rounded kaf in تركنوا, with the latter a dialect form meaning to settle or be content with something.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | Abu Ali discusses a transmitted reading with tanwin on لما and compares it with the phrase أكلا لما, where the verbal noun describes the action.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · علي ابن أبي الطيب | reports | Ali ibn Abi al-Tayyib supplies a fifth analysis with an omitted phrase, وإن كلا لما عملوا ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم, as the poem illustrates ellipsis.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisa'i says he does not know why لما is doubled; Abu Ali accepts that this difficulty is real.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | Abu Ali says the doubled form could mean ما كل إلا ليوفينهم if إن were light and كل nominative, parallel to the cited expression; then لما could more readily be an adjective of indefinite كل. | mentions 43:35
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The syntactic analysis would require كل to be annexed to an indefinite noun so لما can modify it; a definite annexation would block that adjective reading, and no clause element governs it as a circumstantial phrase.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra' takes لما as لمن ما, with one of the three mims deleted, and cites a poetic line.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj takes لما as إلا, but al-Farra' says that use is restricted to oaths, as Abu Ali argues.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · المازني | reports | Al-Mazini says لما is a lightened form that was doubled for emphasis; al-Zajjaj rejects this because Arabic permits weakening a doubled form only under poetic necessity, not doubling a light form.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A fourth proposal derives لما from gathering, builds it on فعلى without declension like تترى, and reads it as all together; al-Zuhri's tanwin reading supports this.
[TABRISI:11:109-112/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن جني | reports | Ibn Jinni parses لما as a comprehensive fulfillment of all their deeds, like using قياما for emphatic emphasis

.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Muhammad is commanded to remain steadfast in preaching and warning, holding to obedience and calling people to practice it as the Qur'an commands; steadfastness means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is prohibited.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas takes those who repented with Muhammad as people who repented from associating partners with God and must also remain steadfast.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another view applies it to all believers who turn back to God and His Prophet; a further parsing has Muhammad maintain delivery while they maintain acceptance.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | They are forbidden to exceed God's command through additions or omissions, which would take them outside steadfastness.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubba'i warns that worldly blessing could make them transgress and leave the bounds of steadfastness.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another gloss says simply not to disobey or oppose God; He sees all their actions and nothing is hidden from Him.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · رسول الله | reports | A report from Umar says even extreme prayer and fasting would not attain steadfastness if people preferred two over one.
[TABRISI:11:112#2/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome on the Prophet than this one; he told his companions that Hud and al-Waqiʿa had made him gray.
[TABRISI:11:112/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Mirya means doubt despite clear evidence; a share is an allotted portion; disagreement can be incompatible opposites or different valid judgments such as facing the qibla; istiqama is staying straight, and transgression exceeds the proper measure in corruption.
[TABRISI:11:112/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | For the experts, doubling the m of لما alongside either doubled or light إن remains problematic: it yields none of the known senses of لم, حين, or إلا.
[TABRISI:11:112/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The related poem uses إلا as an extra particle, meaning the era makes its people confused and leaves petitioners frustrated.
[TABRISI:11:112/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | When إن is light and كل is accusative after a negative sense, the analysis remains difficult; proposals inserting وإن هم إلا or an explanatory كلا are disfavored.
[TABRISI:11:112/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The reading وإن كل إلا ليوفينهم can mean God will certainly repay each one, with إلا treated as an extra particle if إن is lightened.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After the preceding promise and threat, steadfastness is a comprehensive command for creed, practice, and preaching the revelation and laws.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | True steadfastness is hard to discern, like the single boundary between shadow and light that the eye cannot distinguish from either side.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The servant must avoid both anthropomorphism and negation in knowing God and find a difficult middle course between excess and deficiency in anger and desire; remaining on that path is harder still.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says no Qurʾānic verse was harder for the Prophet than this one.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A prophetic report says Sūrat Hūd and its sisters made the Prophet's hair gray; a dream narrative identifies this steadfastness verse as the cause.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The command to be steadfast is a foundational legal principle: follow the stated order in ablution and give like livestock in zakāt, as in all divine commands.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī rejects qualifying a general text by analogy because its clear command must be followed and analogy departs from it.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wāḥidī gives three parses for ومن تاب: coordination with the implied subject of be steadfast, with the subject of “I commanded,” or a new clause meaning the repentant should be steadfast.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A person still in unbelief or sin cannot yet follow the straight path; after repentance, the person can practice the religion and remain in God's service.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “do not transgress” as humility toward God and not acting arrogantly toward anyone.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Other interpretations prohibit distorting the Qurʾān's lawful and unlawful rules, exceeding God's limits, or abandoning gratitude and humility; the author prefers that the phrase include all of them.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Tughyan means exceeding the limit; the prohibition therefore bars transgression. | mentions 69:11
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | An alternative takes the prohibition as a ban on acting arrogantly or oppressively toward anyone.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The command to be steadfast addresses the Prophet and others as well.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says the command addresses the Prophet while intending his community.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Another explanation makes the command a request that God grant steadfastness; the prefix in استقم is like asking God for forgiveness, and steadfastness means staying on one course without deviation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In Muslim, Sufyan ibn Abdullah asks for a concise statement of Islam; the Prophet answers: believe in God, then remain steadfast.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | When Uthman ibn Hadir asked Ibn Abbas for advice, Ibn Abbas urged God-consciousness, steadfastness, following precedent, and avoiding innovation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Those who repented with the Prophet are his companions who left polytheism and later followers of his community; they too must remain steadfast.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome for the Prophet than this one.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | When companions noticed his rapid graying, the Prophet said Hud and its sister surahs had made him gray.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو علي السري | reports | In a dream recounted by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, the Prophet said steadfastness in 11:112, rather than the prophets' stories or peoples' destruction, was what made him gray.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The command follows the account of disagreement over unity and prophecy and the detailed promise and threat; steadfastness covers balanced belief between anthropomorphism and negation, faithful transmission of revelation and law, and proper worship without excess or neglect.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet said that Hud made him gray-haired, alluding to the difficulty of steadfastness.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Those who repented with Muhammad are people who left idolatry and disbelief and believed; the phrase coordinates them with the implied subject of 'be steadfast.'
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Do not go beyond the limits set for you; God sees deeds and will recompense them, which explains both the command and prohibition.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The verse requires following revealed texts without altering or deviating from them through analogy or juristic preference.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The Prophet must remain on the commanded path without deviating; those who repent from disbelief and return sincerely to God are conjoined with him.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The conjunction with the hidden subject is allowed because of the intervening phrase; believers must not cross God's limits, since God sees and recompenses their deeds.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | It is said that no verse was harder for the Prophet than this one, prompting the saying 'Hud has made me gray.'
[QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Those who repent with the Prophet abandon self-assertion and the sin of self-existence, realizing multiplicity within unity and subsistence after annihilation.
[QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r2] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Do not overstep by assigning unqualified divine perfection to the delimited ego, which veils God's identity beyond individuation; God sees whether deeds are through Him or the self.
[QASHANI:11:112-113/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Steadfastness means fulfilling God's rights through God: the Prophet upholds divine commands while witnessing unity after returning to creation, without egoic coloring or neglecting moral duties.
[QASHANI:11:112-113/r2] QASHANI, d. 736 · عليه السلام | reports | The Prophet says that even with divine forgiveness he should remain a grateful servant, after his feet swelled from night worship. | mentions 48:2
[QASHANI:11:112-113/r3] QASHANI, d. 736 · عليه السلام | reports | A report recounts an ʿārif seeing the Prophet ask why Sūrat Hūd had made him gray; the Prop

het says the cause is the command to remain steadfast, not the stories of punished peoples.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عيينة | reports | Ibn ʿUyayna and a group interpret istiqama as remaining firm upon the Quran.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحسن، والأعمش | reports | Al-Hasan and al-Aʿmash read the final phrase with third-person plural verbs, and the reading is also attributed to ʿIsa al-Thaqafi; بصير means God sees their deeds and repays them.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak interprets istiqama as persevering in jihad.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مقاتل | reports | Muqatil says istiqama means continuing upon monotheism.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · جعفر الصادق | reports | Jaʿfar al-Sadiq interprets istiqama as truthful reporting about God with firm resolve.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari glosses the command as maintaining the commanded straightness on the path of truth without departing from it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet was already upright, so the command requires lasting constancy; it addresses him, his believing companions, and the whole community, with the plural form honoring the Prophet.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | استفعل may here express seeking, so istiqama can mean asking to be established in religion; ومن تاب coordinates with the hidden subject after a separator makes explicit reinforcement unnecessary.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains not transgressing as refusing to declare lawful or unlawful anything God did not command.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd says not to transgress means not to disobey the Lord; Muqatil says not to mix monotheism with doubt, and al-Zamakhshari says not to cross God's bounds.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Addressing the Prophet directly in commands to do good, while directing prohibitions to the community, is a mark of eloquence.
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | كما أمرت is accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or as a circumstantial phrase from that noun's pronoun.
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari glosses the command as uprightness like that commanded, remaining on the path of truth without deviation; استقم is a request to maintain uprightness.
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa parses ومن تاب معك as a comitative object, though the author says the resulting meaning is awkward.
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | ومن تاب معك is nominative, coordinated with the hidden subject of استقم; the author follows the clause-level parse and Zamakhshari's sense, you be upright and let your followers be upright. | mentions 2:35
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | reports | The general reading uses the second-person ت in بما تعملون بصير, matching the preceding address.
[SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الحسن والأعمش وعيسى الثقفي | reports | They read بما يعملون with yāʾ, shifting from direct address to third-person reference as in 11:111. | mentions 11:111
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God commands the Messenger and believers to persist in the prescribed straight path; steadfastness is a major aid to victory over enemies and opponents.
